task.pr_title: Adding the initial prototype of a DatabaseLoader

cases.provenance: A human reviewer flagged this defect in an inline comment on the reviewed pull request.
cases.description:
For strings, this type is usually `typeof(ReadOnlyMemory<char>)`. ML.NET uses `ROM<char>` everywhere in order to support sub-strings and not having to allocate each individual string.

We should be sure to add a test for strings to cover this. #Closed

evidence.thread_resolution:
tannergooding: `DbDataReader` does not support `Span` or `ReadOnlyMemory`.
eerhardt: Correct, but ML.NET's IDataView only supports `ReadOnlyMemory<char>` and not `string`. So `TValue` will be of type `ReadOnlyMemory<char>`, and you will need to set the `ref` to the result from `DbDataReader.GetString()`.

See https://github.com/dotnet/machinelearning/blob/45b6c43387294d19cad843a21e87539213e8d34c/src/Microsoft.ML.DataView/DataViewType.cs#L84-L87

When `IDataView` inspects string values, it uses `ReadOnlyMemory<char>`. So you will need to turn the `string` you get from DbDataReader into a `ReadOnlyMemory<char>` here. #Closed
tannergooding: Fixed.
